target.title: fix: emit failover event for successful model fallback chains
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `emitFailoverEvent` was only called from the cooldown/suspend path, so the OTEL `model.failover` diagnostic was never emitted when model fallback actually happened. Multi-hop chains (deepseek-v4-flash → minimax-m2.7 → kimi-k2.6) and all-failed storms were invisible in traces.

**Solution**: Emit a `model.failover` diagnostic event at each failed-candidate → next-candidate transition in the fallback loop. This captures every hop in the chain (from, to, reason, cascade depth) regardless of whether the chain ultimately succeeds or exhausts. The existing `openclaw.failover.*` OTEL attributes already convey fallback occurrence — no undocumented span attribute needed.

**What changed**: `model-fallback.ts`: After recording each failed candidate, emit `model.failover` with `fromProvider/fromModel/toProvider/toModel/reason/cascadeDepth` when a next candidate exists. `diagnostics-otel/service.ts`: Removed new undocumented `has_fallback` attribute (reverted to baseline — existing `openclaw.failover.*` attributes are sufficient).

**What did NOT change**: The cooldown/suspend `emitFailoverEvent` call site. Fallback decision logging. Session suspension. Model candidate resolution.

Fixes #102015

## What Problem This Solves

Model fallback chains happen frequently in production (rate limits, provider outages, model deprecations), but the OTEL `model.failover` diagnostic event was never fired during actual fallback. This prevented operators from detecting retry storms and distinguishing single-model sessions from multi-model cascades.

## Root Cause

`emitFailoverEvent` was only called from one location — the `suspend_lanes` cooldown path. The actual fallback loop (`runWithModelFallbackInternal`) never emitted diagnostics for failed-candidate transitions or successful fallback recoveries.

## Design decision

The emit is placed at the **failed-candidate → next-candidate transition** rather than at success. This covers both all-failed chains (every hop gets a `model.failover` event) and successful chains (the last failed hop before success generates the diagnostic). Success-path emission was removed per review feedback — the transition events already capture the full chain.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `model.failover` diagnostic events fire for each failed-candidate → next-candidate transition in multi-hop fallback chains.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
pnpm test -- src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.probe.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
model-fallback.test.ts        115 passed (115)
model-fallback.probe.test.ts   20 passed (20)
OTEL service.test.ts          107 passed (107)
TOTAL                         242 passed (242)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Each failed-candidate transition in the fallback loop emits a `model.failover` diagnostic event carrying `from/to provider/model`, `reason`, and `cascadeDepth`. The existing cooldown/suspend path is unchanged. 242 existing tests pass without modification.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end OTLP exporter validation requiring a configured telemetry receiver.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — only adds diagnostic event emissions, no behavioral change
- [x] All 242 existing tests pass unchanged
- [x] 2 files, net +0 lines (move from success path to transition point)
- [x] Cooldown/suspend `emitFailoverEvent` call site unchanged
- [x] No new span attributes — existing `openclaw.failover.*` attributes used
- [x] No breaking API changes, no new dependencies
